A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChunkKV. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, chunk-size ablations, and appendix analyses of attention preservation and index reuse.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations involving a 70B model, KIVI quantization, and additional efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged, but v2 adds a procedural variant in Algorithm 3: it budgets selected chunks using Lmax-w and combines them with recent tokens through a selection mask. v1 Algorithm 1 instead budgets using Lmax, then truncates and concatenates. This is a limited algorithmic addition; its use in the retained experiments is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LongBench English and Chinese tasks, NIAH, GSM8K including 50-shot prompting, and JailbreakV. The additions use retained task coverage; the 70B model changes model configuration rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated KIVI quantization comparators in Section 4.5 and Appendix B.6, extending comparison beyond token-eviction methods. Appendix B.7 also adds StreamingLLM and SnapKV to efficiency comparisons that previously reported FullKV and ChunkKV variants. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-3-70B-Instruct evaluation with a 256-token cache, KIVI bit-width configurations, and profiling of prefilling time, cache size, TTFT, and TPOT. These substantially extend evaluation settings and metrics. Existing benchmark settings remain largely intact; the KIVI timing comparison explicitly uses a different software environment.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 extends chunk-size sensitivity evaluation to Mistral on NIAH. Most other analyses are retained or redisplayed: v1's LLaMA chunk-size sweeps become v2 Tables 18–19, while index-reuse and attention-preservation analyses remain available in the appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions with mean scores for general experiments and ten repetitions with average latency and throughput for efficiency experiments. No new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Shared entries in the original main benchmark and timing tables remain unchanged. Substantial new results include the 70B LongBench comparison, where ChunkKV scores 47.24 versus FullKV's 47.15 and SnapKV's 46.11, plus KIVI accuracy and efficiency results in Tables 11 and 22–23. These are additional comparisons, not improvements to the earlier same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C retains the mathematical setup, distinguishability conditions, Lemma 1, Theorem 1, and proof. The index-reuse speedup derivation is also unchanged. Citation and formatting changes do not alter the theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its headline from up to 10% performance improvement to up to 8.7%, described as precision improvement at the same compression ratio. The chunk-preservation and layer-reuse contributions remain unchanged. The 26.5% throughput improvement newly highlighted in the abstract was already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of fragmentation versus overly coarse chunks and discusses eviction–quantization tradeoffs, including code versus single-document QA performance and software-environment comparability. The fixed-size chunking limitation and the qualification concerning incomplete theoretical justification are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.5 documents selection masks, boundary handling, vectorized operations, and PyTorch/CUDA implementation considerations. v2 also discloses KIVI's older-Python dependency and adds JailbreakV's 28,000-test-example dataset statistic. The latter is additional documentation, not evidence of a changed evaluation sample.

R1.justification: v2 adds quantization-related discussion citing KIVI, SmoothQuant, Atom, and FlexGen, plus references to Miller and Ramshaw–Marcus supporting chunking motivation. Existing chunking and layer-wise related-work passages move to Appendix D. The central semantic-preservation positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and substantial experimental discussion, moves related-work passages and the impact statement into appendices, integrates chunk-size ablation into Section 4, and reorganizes the index-reuse appendix. These constitute extensive narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a predominantly single-column layout with wrapped tables. Figure 3 changes from vertically stacked panels to a two-by-two arrangement; ablation displays are merged or relocated, and new implementation and comparison tables are added. Existing heatmaps and most plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The 70B evaluation and KIVI comparisons strengthen evidence about scale and practical alternatives, while Appendix A.5 provides useful implementation guidance. These improve an already extensive empirical study. The gains remain limited by the incompletely specified KIVI software environment and the unreconciled selection procedures in Algorithms 1 and 3; the established main results and theory otherwise remain stable.
